verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Speak to the children of Israel, saying, ‘If anyone sins unintentionally, in any of the things which Yahweh has commanded not to be done, and does any one of them:
if the anointed priest sins so as to bring guilt on the people, then let him offer for his sin, which he has sinned, a young bull without defect to Yahweh for a sin offering.
He shall bring the bull to the door of the Tent of Meeting before Yahweh; and he shall lay his hand on the head of the bull, and kill the bull before Yahweh.
The anointed priest shall take some of the blood of the bull, and bring it to the Tent of Meeting.
The priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle some of the blood seven times before Yahweh, before the veil of the sanctuary.

The priest shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar of sweet incense before Yahweh, which is in the Tent of Meeting; and he shall pour out all of rest of the blood of the bull at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
He shall take all the fat of the bull of the sin offering off of it; the fat that covers the innards, and all the fat that is on the innards,
and the two kidneys, and the fat that is on them, which is by the loins, and the cover on the liver, with the kidneys, he shall take away,
as it is taken off of the bull of the sacrifice of peace offerings. The priest shall burn them on the altar of burnt offering.
The bull’s skin, all its meat, with its head, and with its legs, its innards, and its dung,
he shall carry the whole bull outside of the camp to a clean place, where the ashes are poured out, and burn it on wood with fire. Where the ashes are poured out, it shall be burned.
“‘If the whole congregation of Israel sins, and the thing is hidden from the eyes of the assembly, and they have done any of the things which Yahweh has commanded not to be done, and are guilty;
when the sin in which they have sinned is known, then the assembly shall offer a young bull for a sin offering, and bring it before the Tent of Meeting.
The elders of the congregation shall lay their hands on the head of the bull before Yahweh; and the bull shall be killed before Yahweh.
The anointed priest shall bring of the blood of the bull to the Tent of Meeting:
and the priest shall dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times before Yahweh, before the veil.

He shall put some of the blood on the horns of the altar which is before Yahweh, that is in the Tent of Meeting; and the rest of the blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar of burnt offering, which is at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
All its fat he shall take from it, and burn it on the altar.
Thus shall he do with the bull; as he did with the bull of the sin offering, so shall he do with this; and the priest shall make atonement for them, and they shall be forgiven.
He shall carry the bull outside the camp, and burn it as he burned the first bull. It is the sin offering for the assembly.
“‘When a ruler sins, and unwittingly does any one of all the things which Yahweh his God has commanded not to be done, and is guilty;
if his sin, in which he has sinned, is made known to him, he shall bring as his offering a goat, a male without defect.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the goat, and kill it in the place where they kill the burnt offering before Yahweh. It is a sin offering.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering. He shall pour out the rest of its blood at the base of the altar of burnt offering.
All its fat he shall burn on the altar, like the fat of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin, and he will be forgiven.
“‘If anyone of the common people sins unwittingly, in doing any of the things which Yahweh has commanded not to be done, and is guilty;
if his sin, which he has sinned, is made known to him, then he shall bring for his offering a goat, a female without defect, for his sin which he has sinned.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and kill the sin offering in the place of burnt offering.
The priest shall take some of its blood with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; and the rest of its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.

All its fat he shall take away, like the fat is taken away from off of the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall burn it on the altar for a pleasant aroma to Yahweh; and the priest shall make atonement for him, and he will be forgiven.
“‘If he brings a lamb as his offering for a sin offering, he shall bring a female without defect.
He shall lay his hand on the head of the sin offering, and kill it for a sin offering in the place where they kill the burnt offering.

The priest shall take some of the blood of the sin offering with his finger, and put it on the horns of the altar of burnt offering; and all the rest of its blood he shall pour out at the base of the altar.

All its fat he shall take away, like the fat of the lamb is taken away from the sacrifice of peace offerings; and the priest shall burn them on the altar, on the offerings of Yahweh made by fire; and the priest shall make atonement for him concerning his sin that he has sinned, and he will be forgiven.

footnotes.content: The Lord breaks His silence to instruct Moses again—this time about what happens when we fail, not just when we obey. There is mercy woven into the law itself.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even unintentional sin matters—the heart of Israel is to be guarded, not just the outward act. The Lord knew we would stumble without thinking. He made a way.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A priest's sin weighs heavier because his standing affects the whole people. Even the anointed ones are not above law—they too must come to the altar and lay down their offering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The laying on of hands—that ancient gesture—transfers the guilt from sinner to sacrifice. A human act, witnessed by the Lord, that speaks what words cannot.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The blood brought into the Holy Place—carried by hands that must be clean and careful. Every step toward the sanctuary is an act of mediation, of standing between earth and heaven.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven times—that number again—the priest sprinkles blood before the veil. The number of completion, of God's work. Even our sins are caught up into His pattern.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The horns of the altar where incense rises—the sweetness of prayer touches the place where atonement has been made. Grace and intercession work together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fat—what sustains life, what was most precious—is removed. The offering costs something real, not a token. Sin's forgiveness is never cheap.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Even the kidneys and the cover on the liver—the seat of feeling and thought. Nothing hidden; nothing exempt from this reckoning.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fat rises on the altar of burnt offering—the pleasing aroma that speaks of acceptance. Out of the death of the animal comes a fragrance that reaches heaven.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The skin, meat, head, legs, innards, dung—nothing is spared, nothing withheld. The whole creature is given over, as though it stands in the sinner's place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Outside the camp to a clean place—away from the congregation, yet not lost. The Lord's order shows us that even shame and bearing have their holy place.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When the whole congregation sins and none sees it—a hidden guilt that weighs on all. Yet when it comes to light, there is no hiding from mercy either.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The assembly stands together to bring their offering. In confession, the people are bound—no one alone, no one excused.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The elders lay their hands together on the bull's head. Leadership carries weight—theirs is the hand that must touch this sacrifice for the people's sake.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The anointed priest enters the tent with blood—the mediator taking the people's grief into the sanctuary. His calling is to carry what others cannot.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven sprinklings again before the veil—the people's sin brought to the very edge of God's presence, then answered with mercy, not judgment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The horns of the altar—that gesture of placing sin before the Lord, as if to say: I lay this here. I cannot carry it alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the fat rises to the Lord—even when the whole people sin, the pleasing aroma rises. Forgiveness is complete; the people are not abandoned.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest makes atonement and they shall be forgiven. No lingering stain, no asterisk. The Lord's forgiveness is as thorough as His justice.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The bull carried out as before, burned as the first. The pattern holds whether one priest stumbles or the whole people falters. God's mercy is not rationed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When a ruler sins unintentionally, he is not exempt—authority does not excuse. Yet the grace given him is the same as for all.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A goat instead of a bull—a different offering for a different place in the people. The Lord adjusts His provision, yet the path to forgiveness remains open.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The laying on of hands—the same gesture as for the priest and the congregation. High and low, rich and poor, all meet at this place of confession.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest's finger in the blood, touching the horns of the altar—a smaller offering, yet no less witnessed, no less received.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fat burns and the ruler is forgiven. The word cuts through all his rank and standing. Before the altar, all are leveled and all are lifted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Anyone of the common people—the one no one thinks much about—receives the same care from the Lord's law. His sin counts. His forgiveness is real.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: When his sin is made known, he brings a goat, female without defect. Not what he might choose, but what the Lord has set apart. There is wisdom in prescribed mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: He lays his own hand on his own offering—the poorest among them performs the gesture. His action and God's forgiveness meet.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest's finger touches the altar horns with this person's blood too. In the Lord's sight, no sin is too small to forgive, no penitent too ordinary.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fat burns for a pleasant aroma—even the humble offering rises as a fragrance to heaven. The Lord receives what is offered in faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A lamb may be brought instead—the offering becomes even smaller, even more accessible. The Lord bends low to those with little.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The hand laid on a lamb's head carries the same weight as a hand on a bull. The heart of the matter is confession and trust, not the size of the gift.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The priest's finger and the altar horns—that same image again, the smallest sacrifice given the same ritual care. Nothing offered to the Lord is deemed too little.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The lamb's fat burns as an offering made by fire—and the one who sinned stands forgiven. Readers today hear an echo of grace that meets us not by our status or wealth, but by our willingness to lay our sin before the Lord and trust His mercy.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
